description: Geological lineament data for the Hyderabad metropolitan region. Lineaments represent fractures, faults, and joints in the Archean granite-gneiss basement that control groundwater occurrence. Data compiled from CGWB aquifer mapping reports and GSI geological maps.
source: CGWB Aquifer Mapping Reports, GSI District Resource Maps

zones.name: Hyderabad Urban Core
zones.description: Dense urban granite terrain. Fractures largely sealed by construction. Low effective lineament density due to concretization.
zones.notes: Shallow weathered zone mostly desaturated. Deep fractures at 80-150m may still hold water.

zones.name: Western IT Corridor (Gachibowli-Kondapur-Madhapur)
zones.description: Rapidly urbanized granite terrain. High density of deep borewells competing for limited fracture water.
zones.notes: NW-SE cross-cutting lineaments may hold better yields. Tor formations (boulder hills) indicate deep weathering pockets.

zones.name: Northern Expansion (Bachupally-Dundigal-Kompally)
zones.description: Peri-urban zone with active construction. Granite terrain with moderate fracturing.
zones.notes: Transitional zone. Weathered aquifer still partially saturated in less built-up pockets.

zones.name: Eastern Corridor (Uppal-Ghatkesar-Keesara)
zones.description: Less urbanized granite terrain with better preserved weathered zone. Higher lineament density near the Musi River.
zones.notes: Dolerite dykes act as barriers/conduits depending on orientation. ENE-WSW lineaments aligned with Musi fault zone show higher yields.

zones.name: Southern Rural (Rajendranagar-Maheshwaram-Ibrahimpatnam)
zones.description: Semi-rural granite terrain with thicker weathered zone. Better recharge conditions.
zones.notes: CGWB's Maheshwaram research watershed is located here. Best-studied aquifer system in the Hyderabad region. Shallow borewells (200-400ft) often successful.

zones.name: Western Basalt Cap (Vikarabad-Sangareddy fringe)
zones.description: Deccan Trap basalt overlying granite-gneiss basement. Dual aquifer system.
zones.notes: Basalt vesicular zones hold water near surface. Contact zone between basalt and underlying granite (20-40m depth) is often the best aquifer.
